newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil still seeking alternative to cheque tax.
newsitem.headline: Brazil still seeking alternative to cheque tax.

text.p: The Brazilian government is worried a new tax on financial transactions may hurt stock markets but so far no alternative has been found, Central Bank president Gustavo Loyola said.

"The CPMF (tax) is a very bad tax that brings with it a whole load of problems. But it would also be bad to include lots of exemptions. Managing a tax like that would be very complicated," Loyola told Reuters.
The Provisional Contribution on Financial Movements (CPMF) tax will levy a 0.2 charge on all financial transactions for 12 months from January 23 to raise funds for Brazil's ailing health service.
Government officials and stock market analysts have voiced concern that the new tax may discourage national and foreign investment in stocks.

"I believe the tax could have an impact (on stock markets). It's a worry," Loyola said in an interview. "The ideal solution would be to find another source of funds for the health service and eliminate the CPMF."
Officials were studying the possibility of raising via other taxes the estimated $400 million the CPMF would generate, he said.

Suggestions that foreign investors be exempted from the tax would lead to accusations of priveleged treatment and creating a series of exemptions would make management of the tax impractical, Loyola said.
"There's no point in trying to dress this tax up to make it better because it can't be made better," he said.
